points.why: It describes many agents reacting to each other, with cascades, colliding preferences and convergence on the same slots, but never asks who coordinates or names the absence of a coordinator.
It says the aggregate model will miss interaction effects and recommends an agent-based simulation plus a small, measured pilot.
It proposes tracking combined metrics such as reschedule rate and negotiation rounds, but recommends no hard per-agent limits like reschedule caps, rate limits or unmovable meetings.
It never identifies the centrally designed defaults and limits as the place where IT has leverage.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects the aggregate model because independent decision-makers interact.
